title: Passed pawns

D0.outcome: Explains that a passed pawn has no enemy pawn in front on its own or the adjacent files, and that it is strong only if it can be supported and is not blockaded.

D1.outcome: Identifies passed pawns for both sides, and counts the moves a passed pawn needs against the distance of the enemy king.

D2.outcome: In unlabeled positions, decides whether to push, support or hold back a passed pawn, and notices which enemy piece it ties down.

D3.outcome: Predicts the effect of one-feature changes (a protected pawn, the quality of the blockader, a rook behind it) and says when pushing a passed pawn is premature.

misconceptions: A passed pawn is always strong.
conditions: The pawn's whole path consists of squares the opponent cannot cheaply contest, so he must commit a man to watch it.
A passed pawn gains strength as pieces come off, but blockade, rook-pawns and activity matter.
contrasts: An isolated passed pawn can be a weakness rather than a strength.
Pushing the passer mechanically without asking what it ties down or whether the king can support it.
A passed pawn in a position decided by a king attack.
